title: Indiana Sales Tax Guide: Rates, Compliance, and Regulations for Businesses
summary: We go over Indiana sales tax, including rates, nexus, what's taxable/exempt, and how businesses can stay compliant.
body_markdown:
## Indiana sales tax at a glance


State taxing authority Indiana Department of Revenue


Indiana sales tax rate 7%


Local tax rates None, except for a separate local food and beverage tax in some counties


Combined sales tax rate range 7% statewide


Economic nexus threshold $100,000 in gross revenue with no transaction-count threshold


Website[in.gov/dor](https://www.in.gov/dor/)


Tax line(317) 232-2240


Whether a sale occurs in or ships to Indianapolis, Fort Wayne, or a rural county line, Indiana taxes it at 7%.


Groceries and prescription drugs are broadly exempt, but not every food purchase escapes tax entirely.[Several counties and cities](https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/business-corp/food-and-beverage-tax/) add a separate 1% or 2% tax on prepared food and drinks.


The most common ways businesses establish[nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) are a physical connection to Indiana or gross revenue from Indiana sales exceeding $100,000 in the current or prior calendar year. Indiana dropped its 200-transaction threshold back in 2024.


Businesses remit sales tax through[INTIME](https://intime.dor.in.gov/) , Indiana's online tax portal. They file on the schedule the Department of Revenue assigns.


What gets tricky in Indiana isn't the rate; it's how they tax software. Remotely accessed SaaS and downloaded prewritten software follow two entirely different rules, with SaaS not being taxed while downloaded prewritten software is.


Keep reading to learn more about Indiana sales tax, including rates, what is taxed, how nexus works, and business obligations to stay compliant.

## **Indiana sales tax rates and calculations**


Indiana has a single 7% statewide sales tax rate. No county, city, or special district is allowed to add its own general sales tax on top of it.


The one exception is that several counties and municipalities impose a separate local[food and beverage tax,](https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/business-corp/food-and-beverage-tax/) typically 1% or 2%, on prepared food and drinks sold within their borders.


### **How to calculate Indiana sales tax**


Multiply the taxable sale amount by 7%. A $100 taxable sale anywhere in Indiana carries $7 in sales tax.


### **Origin vs. destination sourcing in Indiana**


In some cases, the seller and the buyer are in different areas of Indiana, or a seller is[outside Indiana](https://www.numeral.com/blog/do-you-charge-sales-tax-on-items-shipped-out-of-state) but selling to a buyer in Indiana. In these situations, you must determine if the buyer’s or the seller's sales tax rules apply.


This is called sourcing. Indiana sources retail sales to the destination, consistent with the[Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/) .


Because the rate is identical statewide, destination sourcing doesn't change what a business owes on a sale. However, it still matters for things like the local food and beverage tax and for keeping Indiana's own sourcing rules consistent with its Streamlined membership.


### **Is Indiana a Streamlined Sales Tax State?**


Yes. Indiana has been a full member of the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement since October 1, 2005, one of the longer-standing members in the program. Remote sellers can register through the[Streamlined Sales Tax system](https://www.sstregister.org/) to cover Indiana, along with other member states, at the same time.


## **Sales tax nexus in Indiana**


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) means you have enough connections with a state that the state can require you to collect sales tax on its behalf.


Before 2018, states couldn’t require out-of-state sellers to charge the state sales tax on online purchases. In[South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that precedent, and states with a sales tax began setting nexus thresholds.


Physical and economic nexus are the two that matter for businesses selling into Indiana.


States each have their own nexus threshold, but generally, a business has[physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) if it has a physical presence in the state, such as an office, warehouse, employees, or inventory.


[Economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) means an out-of-state business meets the dollar limit or transaction limit or both required for charging sales tax to customers in that state.


Nexus Type Threshold


**Physical** Any physical presence in Indiana, including an office, warehouse, distribution center, sales location, or inventory stored at a third-party fulfillment center, even temporarily


**Economic**[Indiana’s economic nexus threshold](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/indiana) is $100,000 in gross revenue from sales into Indiana during the current or previous calendar year, with no separate transaction-count threshold


**Marketplace**[Marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) must register and collect sales tax on behalf of their third-party sellers when they exceed the $100,000 threshold. They must count both direct and facilitated sales toward economic nexus.


**Click-through and affiliate** No thresholds established


### **Economic nexus for remote sellers explained**


Remote sellers have economic nexus in Indiana when they exceed $100,000 in gross revenue from Indiana sales in the current or prior calendar year. Indiana eliminated its 200-transaction backup test on January 1, 2024, so only the dollar figure counts now.


Marketplace-facilitated sales are excluded from a remote seller's own nexus calculation when the facilitator is the one responsible for collecting Indiana tax on those sales.


That means a marketplace-only seller generally doesn't need to register in Indiana solely because the platform already handles those sales.


Once the threshold is crossed through direct sales, though, registration should happen before the next taxable sale.


## **What's taxable and exempt in Indiana**


Category Taxable? Notes


**Tangible personal property** Yes Most physical goods are taxable unless specifically exempt


**Groceries** No Most food for off-premises consumption is exempt; prepared food is taxable


**Clothing and footwear** Yes No standing exemption


**Prescription drugs** No Fully exempt


**SaaS or remotely accessed software** Generally no Nontaxable when the customer does not obtain a possessory interest in the software


**Downloaded prewritten software** Yes Taxable when delivered electronically to the customer


**Specified digital products** Yes Includes digital audio, audiovisual works and digital books


**Services** Generally no Most services are exempt unless tied to a taxable good


**Shipping** Yes Generally taxable when tied to a taxable sale, regardless of how it is stated on the invoice


### **What's subject to sales tax in Indiana**


- Most retail sales of tangible personal property
- Prepared food, and prepared food or beverages sold in a county or city that also levies a local food and beverage tax
- Downloaded prewritten software and[specified digital products](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) , including digital audio, audiovisual works, and digital books
- Telecommunications services and a short list of other enumerated services


### **What's exempt from sales tax in Indiana**


- Most groceries purchased for home or off-premises consumption
- Prescription drugs and certain medical equipment
- Sales for resale backed by a valid exemption certificate
- Qualifying purchases by nonprofit organizations and government entities


### **SaaS taxability in Indiana**


Indiana draws a line between software you access remotely and software you actually download, and the two get taxed differently.


- **Pure remote access** , where the customer logs into software the provider hosts and never obtains a possessory interest in it, is generally not taxable.
- **Downloaded prewritten software** works the opposite way and is generally taxable once it's delivered electronically to the customer.
- **Mixed transactions** , where a deal bundles remote access with some downloaded component, can require a closer look rather than a simple yes-or-no answer.


[Our Indiana SaaS sales tax guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-indiana) walks through the distinction in more depth.


### **Digital products are a separate category**


[Digital products](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) shouldn't get lumped in with the SaaS discussion, because Indiana taxes them under their own rule. Electronically transferred products are taxable only when they fall into specific categories: specified digital products, prewritten software, or telecommunications services.


Specified digital products cover things like digital audio, audiovisual works, and digital books, the kind of permanent, one-time digital purchase that's different from a SaaS subscription.


### **Resale and exemption certificates in Indiana**


Indiana buyers use[Form ST-105](https://www.in.gov/dor/tax-forms/business/sales-tax-forms/) , the General Sales Tax Exemption Certificate, to purchase for[resale](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) or another exempt purpose.


The form has no fixed[expiration date](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-exemption-certificate-expiration-by-state) , but it's only valid while the buyer's Registered Retail Merchant Certificate or exemption status stays active, so buyers need their Registered Retail Merchant Certificate number to claim resale.


Out-of-state buyers can use ST-105 with their home state's tax ID or the[Streamlined Certificate of Exemption](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/docs/default-source/forms/exemption-certificateb926a7ab4a0d43e1ad4fe8eb19e79cbb.pdf?sfvrsn=857843d_7) . Keep certificates for at least three years.


## **Registering for an Indiana sales tax license**


Indiana calls its permit a Registered Retail Merchant Certificate, issued after registering through the[INBiz](https://inbiz.in.gov/) portal, the state's online business registration system. There's a $25 fee per registered location, nonrefundable regardless of the outcome, and paper applications are no longer accepted.


Have your EIN or SSN, business address, owner and officer details, and NAICS code ready. There's no separate local sales tax registration. Businesses selling food and beverages in a county or city with a food and beverage tax add that registration through the same process.


A Registered Retail Merchant Certificate is valid for two years, and the Department of Revenue renews it automatically at no cost as long as the business is current on its returns and payments. It must be displayed at each business location, as in most other states.


### **Registration requirements for remote sellers**


Remote sellers register through that same INBiz process once Indiana sales cross the $100,000 threshold. Collection should begin with the next taxable sale after the threshold is crossed, not after registration paperwork clears, so it's worth registering as soon as the number is in sight rather than waiting.


Remote sellers can also register through the[Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System](https://www.sstregister.org/) instead of INBiz.


## **Collecting Indiana sales tax**


With a flat statewide rate, collecting Indiana sales tax is about as simple as it gets. Confirm the sale is taxable, apply 7%, collect it at checkout, and keep the record for the return.


### **Marketplace sales**


Marketplace facilitators whose own and facilitated sales into Indiana clear $100,000 must register and collect on behalf of their third-party sellers. Those facilitated sales count toward a seller's own economic nexus calculation.


However, direct sales made outside the marketplace, through a seller's own site, still count and still need to be collected on.


A seller with inventory sitting in an Indiana fulfillment center has physical nexus regardless of how the marketplace handles tax on facilitated sales, so it's worth tracking inventory locations separately from the sales channel.


### **Shipping and delivery charges**


[Delivery and shipping charges are generally taxable](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) in Indiana when they're tied to a taxable sale, whether or not the charge is broken out separately on the invoice.


Selling a mix of taxable and exempt items in one order means you should prorate the shipping charge between the two, with tax applying only to the portion tied to the taxable goods.


Two exceptions: separately stated U.S. Postal Service postage isn't taxable, and neither is a delivery charge billed directly to the customer by a third-party carrier.


## **Filing and paying Indiana sales tax**


The Department of Revenue assigns a[filing frequency](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-due-dates) , generally monthly or annual, based on a business's tax liability, and returns get filed through[INTIME](https://intime.dor.in.gov/) . Returns are typically due the 20th of the month following the reporting period, though businesses with lower annual liability may be assigned the 30th instead.


Zero returns are still required in periods with no taxable sales. Indiana offers a small collection allowance for on-time filers, applied automatically when a return is filed and paid by the due date.


### **Filing Indiana sales tax online**


All Indiana sales tax returns are filed electronically through[INTIME](https://intime.dor.in.gov/) , which replaced the state's older INtax system. Registration, filing, and payment all live in the same portal.


Our[guide to filing Indiana sales tax](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-indiana-sales-tax-online) walks through the process step by step.


## **Indiana sales tax penalties and interest**


[A late return or late payment](https://www.numeral.com/blog/what-happens-if-you-dont-collect-or-remit-sales-tax) carries a penalty of 10% of the tax due, or $5, whichever is greater. A late zero return draws its own penalty of $10 per day the return is overdue, capped at $250, and a bounced payment brings a flat $35 fee on top of everything else.


Interest accrues on unpaid tax from the original due date at a rate the Department of Revenue sets annually; the underpayment rate for 2026 is 7%. Fraud carries a separate penalty of 100% of the underpayment, on top of whatever tax was actually owed.


## **Indiana sales tax recordkeeping and audits**


Businesses should keep sales records, exemption certificates, and returns on file to support what they reported, since the Department of Revenue[can audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) a business to verify taxability calls, exemptions claimed, and whether the correct amount got collected and remitted.


Indiana requires records to be kept for at least three years after the tax was due, or indefinitely if a return was never filed.


A business has 60 days from a proposed assessment to[file a written protest](https://www.in.gov/dor/resources/legal/appeals/) with the Department, and that deadline can't be extended. If the Department's Letter of Findings still doesn't resolve things, the next step is an appeal to the Indiana Tax Court within 90 days.

## **Indiana sales tax FAQs**


**What is the sales tax rate in Indiana?**


A flat 7% statewide. No county or city adds a general local sales tax on top of it, though some jurisdictions add a separate local tax on prepared food and beverages.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in Indiana?**


$100,000 in gross revenue from sales into Indiana in the current or previous calendar year. There's no separate transaction-count threshold anymore.


**Are services taxable in Indiana?**


[Most services are exempt from sales tax](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-services) unless they involve transferring tangible personal property or fall into a short list of taxable categories, like telecommunications.


**Is SaaS taxable in Indiana?**


[SaaS is not taxable in Indiana](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-indiana) when customers access the software online without taking possession of it. Prewritten software that customers download is usually taxable.


**Are digital products taxable in Indiana?**


Yes, when they qualify as specified digital products, like digital audio, video, or books, or as prewritten software or telecommunications services.


**Does Indiana charge sales tax on shipping and delivery?**
Yes, generally, when the charge is tied to a taxable sale. Separately stated U.S. Postal Service postage and delivery billed directly by a third-party carrier are exempt.


**Do I need a sales tax permit in Indiana?**


Yes, once physical or economic nexus applies. Registration happens online through INBiz for a Registered Retail Merchant Certificate.


**Do marketplace sellers need to collect sales tax in Indiana?**


Not on sales a marketplace facilitator already collects above Indiana's threshold. Those facilitated sales are also excluded from the seller's own nexus calculation, though direct sales still count and still need to be collected on.


**How often do businesses need to file sales tax returns in Indiana?**


Monthly or annually, generally, based on the tax liability the Department of Revenue assigns after registration.


**Are groceries and clothing taxable in Indiana?**


Groceries for home or off-premises consumption are exempt, though prepared food is taxable. Clothing has no exemption and is taxed like any other retail good.
